families.title: Discover
families.text: Find datasets and variables and read their documentation.

functions.name: datasets
functions.summary: The catalog: one row per dataset and scale.
functions.returns:
Columns ``dataset`` (the id to pass to ``geo.load``), ``scale``, ``title``,
``years`` (e.g. ``"2001–2020"`` for an annual panel or ``"2012, 2024"`` for two
periods), ``units`` (units with data), ``variables`` (how many), ``first_year``,
``last_year``, ``license``, ``categories`` and the ``csv`` and ``parquet`` paths.

functions.name: search
functions.summary: Find variables whose name, label or description contain every word of ``text``.
functions.body:
Matching ignores case and accents (``"educacion"`` finds "Educación"). Results
are ranked: matches in the variable name or label come first.

params.name: text
params.text: one or more words, e.g. ``"poverty"`` or ``"night lights"``

params.name: dataset
params.text: search only this dataset

functions.returns:
One row per variable and scale: ``dataset``, ``variable``, ``label``, ``unit``,
``years``, ``scale``, ``units`` (with data) and ``description``. Pass the
``dataset`` and ``variable`` to ``geo.load(dataset, variables=variable)``.

functions.name: info
functions.summary: What a dataset is: description, coverage (scales, units, years), actual reference years, license, sources with their licenses, citation, notes and notebooks.

params.name: dataset
params.text: dataset id (see ``geo.datasets()``)

functions.returns:
A ``DatasetInfo``: in a notebook it displays as formatted HTML; ``print()``
gives plain text, and ``.dict`` the full datapackage.

functions.name: dictionary
functions.summary: The variable dictionary of a dataset, one row per column.

params.name: dataset
params.text: dataset id (see ``geo.datasets()``)

params.name: scale
params.text: the resource's scale (default: the dataset's native scale)

functions.returns:
Columns ``variable``, ``label`` (the field's ``title``, a readable name for
plot axes and legends), ``description`` (how it was built), ``unit``, ``role``
(id, time, source_key or variable), ``aggregation`` (the rule ``geo.aggregate``
uses), ``source`` and ``reference_years`` (the actual years behind each stored
year, e.g. ``"2012: 2008; 2024: 2023"``, when they differ).

functions.name: reference_years
functions.summary: The actual years behind each stored year, one row per variable and stored year.
functions.body:
Some panels store values at nominal years: the SDG Atlas, for example, stores its
initial values at 2012 and its final values at 2024, while an indicator may come
from a survey of 2008 and 2023.

params.name: dataset
params.text: dataset id

params.name: variable
params.text: one variable (default: all)

params.name: scale
params.text: the resource's scale (default: the dataset's native scale)

functions.returns:
Columns ``variable``, ``label``, ``year`` (as stored) and ``reference`` (the
actual years; the stored year when they are the same).

functions.name: cite
functions.summary: How to cite a dataset: its recommended citation, then the credits its sources require.

params.name: dataset
params.text: dataset id

params.name: style
params.text: ``"apa"`` (plain text) or ``"bibtex"``

families.title: Load
families.text: Panels, units, boundaries and crosswalks, from GitHub or a local checkout.

functions.name: load
functions.signature: load(dataset, scale=None, years=None, variables=None, wide=None, geometry=False, names=False, groups=None, ref=None)
functions.summary: Load a dataset as a panel: one row per unit (``geo_id``) and year.

params.name: dataset
params.text: dataset id (see ``geo.datasets()``)

params.name: scale
params.text: scale to load; defaults to the dataset's native scale

params.name: years
params.text: an int, a list of ints, or a ``(first, last)`` range (inclusive)

params.name: variables
params.text: a variable or list of variables to keep (``geo_id`` and ``year`` are always kept); ``geo.search()`` and ``geo.dictionary()`` list them

params.name: wide
params.text: a variable name; returns one row per unit with one column per year (``<variable><year>``)

params.name: geometry
params.text: attach unit boundaries (and names) and return a GeoDataFrame

params.name: names
params.text: add the unit ``name``

params.name: groups
params.text: coarser scales whose unit names to add as columns, e.g. ``["department"]`` adds a ``department`` column (implies ``names``)

params.name: ref
params.text: git branch, tag or commit to read from GitHub (default: local checkout or ``main``)

functions.notes:
Raises ``ValueError`` for unknown variables, and for years that have no rows
(listing the years the dataset has).

functions.name: units
functions.summary: All units (or the units of one scale) with names, parents and source keys.

params.name: scale
params.text: a scale id (see ``geo.scales()``); default: every scale

functions.returns:
Every row has ``geo_id``, ``scale``, ``name``, ``parent_id``, ``area_km2``, a
``<scale>_id`` column for each coarser scale it lies in, and the codes each
source uses for it (e.g. ``ine_code``), which ``geo.link(..., key=...)`` matches.

functions.name: boundaries
functions.summary: Unit polygons for a scale (CRS84), with ``geo_id`` and ``name``.

params.name: scale
params.text: a scale id (see ``geo.scales()``)

functions.name: crosswalk
functions.summary: Links between two scales: ``geo_id_from``, ``geo_id_to``, ``weight_area``.

params.name: source
params.text: the finer scale, e.g. ``"municipality"``

params.name: target
params.text: a coarser scale it nests in, e.g. ``"department"``

functions.returns:
``weight_area`` is the share of the source unit's area inside the target unit
(1.0 for nested scales). Crosswalks are published for every pair of active
scales where one nests in the other, from finer to coarser.

functions.name: scales
functions.summary: The registry of spatial scales as a table, one row per scale (``geo.scales()``).
functions.body:
Columns: ``label``, ``kind`` (admin, grouping, grid, custom), ``parent`` (the
coarser scale it nests in), ``children``, ``id_pattern``, ``example`` and
``status`` (active or planned). ``active_only=True`` hides planned scales.

functions.name: ancestors
functions.summary: Coarser scales a unit of ``scale`` nests in, in breadth-first order.
functions.body:
Administrative scales follow ``parent``; a scale whose units are unions of
``scale`` units (a grouping, such as statistical regions) is also an ancestor. The parent
chain of each level comes before the groupings of that level, e.g.
``municipality -> [province, department, country]``.

functions.name: scale_of
functions.summary: The scale a geo ID belongs to, from the ID patterns (e.g. a municipality ID -> ``"municipality"``).

functions.name: config
functions.summary: The contents of project.yaml.

families.title: Understand
families.text: Labels, summaries, change between periods and quick maps.

functions.name: labels
functions.summary: Readable labels for the columns of a panel (or every field of a dataset id).
functions.body:
Variables take their metadata ``title``; columns written by ``geo.change()``
(``<var>_2024``, ``<var>_change``...) are labelled from their variable; group
columns (``department``) take the scale's label.

params.name: data
params.text: a panel (any DataFrame) or a dataset id

functions.returns:
``{column: label}`` for the columns it knows. Pass it to Plotly:
``px.scatter(df, x=..., y=..., labels=geo.labels(df))``.

functions.name: describe
functions.summary: Summary statistics of a panel's variables, per ``by`` group (default: per year).

params.name: df
params.text: a panel, e.g. from ``geo.load``

params.name: variables
params.text: a variable or list of them (default: every numeric variable)

params.name: by
params.text: a column to group by: ``"year"`` (default), ``None`` to pool all rows, or a group such as ``"department"`` (after ``geo.load(..., groups=["department"])``)

functions.returns:
One row per variable (and group): ``variable``, ``label``, ``unit``, ``count``,
``mean``, ``std``, ``min``, ``p25``, ``median``, ``p75`` and ``max``.

functions.name: add_names
functions.summary: Add the unit ``name`` and, for each scale in ``groups``, the name of the unit it lies in.

params.name: df
params.text: any table with ``geo_id``

params.name: groups
params.text: a coarser scale or list of them (see ``geo.ancestors``), e.g. ``["department"]``

params.name: scale
params.text: the units' scale (default: inferred from ``geo_id``)

functions.returns:
A copy with ``name`` and one column per group (the group unit's name) after
``geo_id`` (and ``year``).

functions.name: change
functions.summary: The change of each unit between two years of a panel, one row per unit.

params.name: df
params.text: a long panel with ``geo_id``, ``year`` and variables (e.g. from ``geo.load``)

params.name: variables
params.text: a variable or list of them (default: every numeric variable)

params.name: first, last
params.text: the two years to compare (default: the panel's first and last year)

functions.returns:
One row per unit. For each variable ``v``: ``v_<first>``, ``v_<last>``,
``v_change`` (last minus first), ``v_pct_change`` (in percent of the first
value), ``v_annual_change`` (the change divided by the years between them),
``v_rank_<first>`` and ``v_rank_<last>`` (1 = highest value) and
``v_rank_change`` (positive when the unit climbed). Text columns that are
constant within a unit (``name``, ``department``...) are kept.

The years are the stored years: for panels stored at nominal years (see
``geo.reference_years``), the actual span of an indicator may differ.

functions.name: map
functions.signature: map(data, variable, year=None, scale=None, title=None, simplify=0.005, ref=None, **kwargs)
functions.summary: An interactive choropleth map (Plotly) of one variable in one year.

params.name: data
params.text: a dataset id, or a panel with ``geo_id`` (with or without geometry), e.g. from ``geo.load``, ``geo.change`` or ``geo.aggregate``

params.name: variable
params.text: the column to colour by

params.name: year
params.text: the year to map (default: the last year with data); ignored for tables without a ``year`` column

params.name: scale
params.text: the units' scale (default: inferred from ``geo_id``)

params.name: title
params.text: the figure title (default: the variable's label and the year)

params.name: simplify
params.text: tolerance in degrees for simplifying the drawn boundaries (about 500 m by default, invisible at the country's scale; it keeps the figure light). ``None`` draws them in full detail

params.name: **kwargs
params.text: passed to ``plotly.express.choropleth_map`` (e.g. ``color_continuous_scale="Viridis"``, ``range_color=(0, 100)``)

functions.returns:
Returns a ``plotly.graph_objects.Figure``; it displays in a notebook, and
``.show()`` displays it from a script or a cell that does more afterwards.

families.title: Move across scales
families.text: Up the hierarchy with each variable's rule, or onto units that do not nest.

functions.name: aggregate
functions.signature: aggregate(df, to, dataset=None, rules=None, variables=None, weights=None, ref=None)
functions.summary: Aggregate a panel up to a coarser, nested scale (or to several at once).

params.name: df
params.text: panel with ``geo_id``, optionally ``year``, and variable columns

params.name: to
params.text: target scale id, or a list of them (e.g. ``["department", "country"]``), each containing the source scale (see ``geo.ancestors``)

params.name: dataset
params.text: take each variable's ``geo:aggregation`` rule from this dataset's metadata

params.name: rules
params.text: explicit rules that override the metadata, e.g. ``{"y": "weighted_mean:pop"}``

params.name: variables
params.text: variables to aggregate (default: every numeric column except ids and year, leaving out, with a warning, those without a rule)

params.name: weights
params.text: extra columns to join on ``geo_id`` (and ``year`` if present) for ``weighted_mean`` rules whose weight is not already in ``df``. When the dataset's metadata names where a weight lives (``geo:weights``, e.g. census population), it is loaded automatically.

functions.returns:
Returns one row per target unit (and year) with ``n_units``, the number of
source units that contributed, and ``coverage``, their share of all the source
units in the target (1.0 when every unit has data). With a list of targets,
the results are stacked with a ``scale`` column.

functions.name: combine
functions.signature: combine(datasets, scale, years=None, extra=(), rules=None, ref=None)
functions.summary: Merge datasets into one panel at ``scale``, aggregating finer ones up.

params.name: datasets
params.text: dataset ids, or ``{dataset: [variables]}`` to pick variables

params.name: scale
params.text: target scale; each dataset must be published at it or nest in it

params.name: years
params.text: as in ``geo.load``

params.name: extra
params.text: your own panels (with ``geo_id`` and ``year``) at ``scale``

params.name: rules
params.text: aggregation rules overriding the metadata, ``{variable: rule}``

functions.notes:
Variables without an aggregation rule (``none``) are dropped, with a warning,
when a dataset has to be aggregated. Clashing column names get the dataset
id as a prefix (``<dataset>_<column>``). Weighted means fetch their weights as
``geo.aggregate()`` does (``geo:weights`` in the metadata).

functions.name: overlay
functions.signature: overlay(df, target, extensive=(), intensive=(), source=None, id_col='geo_id')
functions.summary: Area-weighted interpolation of a panel onto non-nested units.

params.name: df
params.text: panel with ``geo_id``, optionally ``year``, and the variables

params.name: target
params.text: a scale id or a GeoDataFrame with ``id_col`` and polygons (e.g. a grid)

params.name: extensive
params.text: counts/totals (population, GDP): split by the share of each source unit's area falling in the target, then summed

params.name: intensive
params.text: rates/averages (GDP per capita, HDI): area-weighted mean over the parts of source units inside the target

params.name: source
params.text: the source scale or GeoDataFrame (default: inferred from ``geo_id``)

functions.notes:
Assumes values are spread uniformly within each source unit. Returns one row
per target unit (and year), with ``geo_id`` holding the target ids.

functions.name: overlay_weights
functions.summary: Area of every source-target intersection, in an equal-area projection.

params.name: source, target
params.text: scale ids, or GeoDataFrames with ``id_col`` and polygons

params.name: id_col
params.text: the id column of GeoDataFrame inputs

functions.returns:
Columns ``geo_id_from``, ``geo_id_to``, ``area_km2``, ``share_of_from`` (the
part of the source unit inside the target) and ``share_of_to``.

families.title: Build
families.text: Link your own data, extract indicators from rasters, check and save them.

functions.name: link
functions.signature: link(df, scale, on, key='auto', errors='raise', ref=None)
functions.summary: Attach ``geo_id`` to a table that identifies units by name or by a source code.

params.name: df
params.text: your table (one row per unit, or per unit and year)

params.name: scale
params.text: scale of your units, e.g. ``"province"`` (see ``geo.scales()``)

params.name: on
params.text: the column of ``df`` that identifies the unit

params.name: key
params.text: the column of ``geo.units(scale)`` to match against: ``"name"``, a source code column of ``geo.units(scale)`` (e.g. ``"gid"`` for GADM codes), or ``"auto"``: the column matching most values, with the others filling the gaps (so mixed spellings from different sources still link). Matching ignores accents, case, spaces and punctuation ("BântéayMéanchey" = "Banteay Meanchey"). A value shared by several units (two municipalities with the same name) is ambiguous and links to none of them: link such units by a code instead.

params.name: errors
params.text: ``"raise"`` (default), ``"warn"`` or ``"ignore"`` for values that match no unit or are ambiguous

functions.returns: Returns a copy of ``df`` with ``geo_id`` as its first column.

functions.name: check
functions.summary: Problems that would stop ``df`` from being a valid panel at ``scale`` (empty list = OK).
functions.body:
Checks: a ``geo_id`` column, ids known at the scale, one row per unit (and
year) and integer years.

params.name: df
params.text: your panel, e.g. from ``geo.link``

params.name: scale
params.text: its scale (default: inferred from ``geo_id``)

params.name: time
params.text: the year column, or ``None`` for a cross-section

functions.name: zonal
functions.signature: zonal(raster, scale, stats=('sum', 'mean'), name='value', year=None, band=1, all_touched=False, ref=None)
functions.summary: Summarise a raster (GeoTIFF path or URL) over the units of a scale.

params.name: raster
params.text: path or URL of a raster, or ``{year: path}`` for an annual series

params.name: scale
params.text: a scale id, or a GeoDataFrame with ``geo_id`` and polygons

params.name: stats
params.text: any of ``sum``, ``mean``, ``min``, ``max``, ``median``, ``count``

params.name: name
params.text: prefix of the output columns (``name_sum``, ``name_mean``, ...)

params.name: year
params.text: year to record when ``raster`` is a single file

params.name: all_touched
params.text: count every pixel a unit touches (default: pixel centres inside)

functions.notes:
Needs ``rasterio``: in Colab, ``!pip install -q "geo4bolivia[raster]"``.
Pixels are not split at unit edges, so use a fine raster, or
``all_touched=True`` for very small units. Nodata pixels are ignored.

functions.name: save
functions.signature: save(df, name, scale, directory='.', title=None, description='', variables=None, sources=(), citation=None, license='CC-BY-4.0')
functions.summary: Save a panel exactly like the published datasets, ready to share or contribute.

params.name: df
params.text: a valid panel (see ``geo.check``)

params.name: name
params.text: the dataset id: lowercase letters, digits, ``-`` or ``_``

params.name: scale
params.text: its scale

params.name: directory
params.text: where to write ``data/`` and ``metadata/`` (default: the current folder)

params.name: title, description
params.text: what the dataset is

params.name: variables
params.text: ``{column: {"label", "description", "unit", "aggregation", "source"}}``

params.name: sources
params.text: titles or ``{"title", "path"}`` dicts of the sources

params.name: citation
params.text: the recommended citation

params.name: license
params.text: an SPDX license id (default ``CC-BY-4.0``)

functions.notes:
Writes ``<directory>/data/<scale>/<name>.csv`` and ``.parquet`` and
``<directory>/metadata/<name>.datapackage.json`` (Frictionless). Describe each
variable in ``variables``: ``{"pop": {"label": "Population", "description":
"Sum of WorldPop 100 m population over the unit", "unit": "people",
"aggregation": "sum", "source": "WorldPop"}}``. The ``label`` is a readable
name for plots; the description says how the variable was built. The
aggregation rule (``sum``, ``mean``, ``weighted_mean:<field>``, ``none``, ...)
tells ``geo.aggregate()`` how to move the variable to coarser scales.

Returns the datapackage as a dict.

families.title: Analyse
families.text: Labelled inputs for the companion packages.

functions.name: for_expdpy
functions.signature: for_expdpy(data, scale=None, years=None, variables=None, labels=None, groups=None, ref=None)
functions.summary: ``(df, df_def)`` in the format expdpy expects.

params.name: data
params.text: a dataset id or your own panel with ``geo_id`` and ``year``

params.name: scale, years, variables
params.text: as in ``geo.load`` (for a dataset id)

params.name: labels
params.text: ``{variable: description}`` for your own columns

params.name: groups
params.text: coarser scales whose unit names to add as columns

functions.returns:
df : the panel with ``geo_id``, ``name``, ``year``, the group names and the variables
df_def : the data dictionary (``var_name``, ``var_def``, ``label``, ``type``,
    ``role``, ``can_be_na``); pass both to ``ex.set_labels(df, df_def, set_panel=True)``
functions.notes:
These are the parameters of ``for_geometrics``. ``groups`` is handy for expdpy's
by-group views, e.g. ``groups=["department"]`` adds a ``department`` column
(the department's name) for ``ex.explore_trend_plot_by_group``.

functions.name: for_geometrics
functions.signature: for_geometrics(data, scale=None, years=None, variables=None, labels=None, groups=None, ref=None)
functions.summary: ``(gdf, df, df_dict)`` in the format geometrics expects.

params.name: data
params.text: a dataset id (see ``geo.datasets()``) or your own panel with ``geo_id`` and ``year`` (from ``geo.link``, ``geo.combine``, ``geo.zonal``...)

params.name: scale, years, variables
params.text: as in ``geo.load`` (for a dataset id)

params.name: labels
params.text: ``{variable: description}`` for your own columns (dataset variables are described from the metadata)

params.name: groups
params.text: coarser scales whose unit names to add as columns, e.g. ``["province"]``

functions.returns:
gdf : GeoDataFrame with ``geo_id`` and ``geometry`` (EPSG:4326)
df : the panel with ``geo_id``, ``name``, ``year``, the group names and the variables
df_dict : one row per ``df`` column with ``var_name``, ``var_def``, ``label``,
    ``type`` (entity / time / factor / numeric), ``role`` and ``can_be_na``
